{{Recipe}}

'''Beurre monté''' is a French sauce with many applications; it can be used plain as a dip, cooked in, or adjusted with savory or sweet ingredients. The sauce is simply an emulsion of butter into water, which gives butter a saucier consistency. It can act as a base sauce, meaning ingredients can be added to enhance its flavor, or it can be served plain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Masterclass |date=5 June 2024 |title=Beurre Monté Recipe: How to Make Emulsified Butter Sauce |url=https://www.masterclass.com/articles/how-to-make-beurre-monte |url-status=live |access-date=15 June 2024 |website=masterclass.com}}</ref> It acts as a sister sauce of [[Cookbook:Beurre Blanc|beurre blanc]], which emulsifies the butter in reduced white wine and vinegar.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Claiborne and Franey |first=C. |date=16 June 2024 |title=Beurre Blanc Classic French Butter sauce |url=https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/2020-beurre-blanc-classic-french-butter-sauce |url-status=live |access-date=16 June 2024 |website=cooking.nytimes.com}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==

* 3 parts by weight of water
* 8 parts by weight of [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], cold
* Seasoning, as desired

== Procedure ==
# Bring the water to a low [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in an appropriately sized cooking vessel, such as a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
# Add butter, gradually [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisking]] until smoothly incorporated. Make sure the butter is completely emulsified in before adding the next chunk.
# Season to taste as desired.
# Keep warm until use. Don't overheat, as this will break the emulsion.
